originality.rationale: Meyer and Schmidt already analyze the same square-with-center four-equal-plus-central-mass family and identify its unique degeneracy at the exact mass \((13+11\sqrt2)/12\), with kite and trapezoid branches at that degeneracy and no nonsymmetric relative equilibria bifurcating from the square family. Since this mass is about \(2.38\), their result directly implies nondegeneracy and absence of bifurcation throughout \([1,2]\). The audited interval result is therefore a special-case corollary of stronger prior coverage.
residual_risks: The prior paper uses relative-equilibrium language and its own normalization, but the square-plus-central-mass family and degeneracy parameter are the same mathematical object.
